title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Sherry and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Sherry labels name the style: Fino, Manzanilla, Amontillado, Oloroso, Palo Cortado, Cream or PX. Look for en rama, an age statement like VOS or VORS, or 12 or 15 year old Sherry. Manzanilla always comes from Sanlúcar. Most Sherry has no vintage, being a solera blend; añada Sherries are rare single vintages.

steps.title: Serving
steps.body: Serve Fino and Manzanilla well chilled, 6 to 8 degrees, in a white wine glass; keep open bottles in the fridge and finish within a week. Amontillado and Palo Cortado at 12 to 14; Oloroso at 14 to 16; PX slightly cool. Oxidative styles keep for weeks once open.

options: Well chilled, and finished within a week
After years in an open bottle
steps.explanation: Fino is delicate; serve it cold and fresh.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Fino and Manzanilla suit tapas: olives, almonds, jamón, fried fish, prawns. Amontillado suits soups, mushrooms and tricky vegetables like artichokes and asparagus. Oloroso suits stews, game and hard cheese. PX suits vanilla ice cream, blue cheese and chocolate.

steps.prompt: Which foods suit Fino or Manzanilla?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels name the style and sometimes an age
Serve Fino cold and fresh; Oloroso cool
Fino with tapas, Amontillado with soups, PX with ice cream
